script.title: DBMS Normalization: First Normal Form
learningObjectives: Identify repeating groups that violate first normal form

sections.heading: Why normalize?
sections.explanation: Normalization organizes relational data to reduce unnecessary duplication and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.
sections.example: Storing a customer's phone numbers in a repeated comma-separated field makes searching and updating individual numbers difficult.

sections.heading: First normal form
sections.explanation: A relation is in first normal form when each row-column intersection contains one atomic value and repeating groups are removed.
sections.example: Instead of Phone1 and Phone2 columns, store one phone number per row in a related customer-phone table.

keyTakeaways: Normalization reduces redundancy and common data anomalies.
First normal form requires atomic values and no repeating groups.

scenes.title: Normalization
scenes.narration: Learn why relational tables are normalized and what first normal form requires.

scenes.title: Remove repeating values
scenes.narration: A customer row with several phone numbers in one cell contains a repeating group. Split the values into individual rows linked to the customer.

scenes.title: Quick recall
scenes.narration: A table stores three phone numbers in one cell separated by commas. Which normalization rule is being violated?
